findings.title: order() mixin is off by one for the 2009 flexbox syntax
findings.body: The order() mixin copies $val verbatim into -webkit-box-ordinal-group/-moz-box-ordinal-group, but the 2009 syntax is 1-based (default ordinal-group is 1 and values < 1 are invalid) while flex order is 0-based (default 0). To emulate order:N on old WebKit/Firefox the ordinal-group must be N+1. As written, order(0) would be invalid/dropped and ordered items are shifted one group toward unordered items, so the legacy-prefixed rendering this mixin exists for (used by .panel order(3) in header.scss and .extra-info-wrapper order(2) in topic.scss) can order header children differently from the standard `order` rendering.

findings.title: Flex .small-action loses the right-aligned action button
findings.body: Making .small-action a flex container (lines 264-265) makes float have no effect on its flex items, including the direct-child button styled `float: right` at lines 306-310. No replacement positioning is added (no margin-left: auto on the button, no justify-content, and .small-action-desc has no flex-grow), so the button that was previously pinned to the right edge of the row now sits immediately after the description text, changing the layout of small-action rows (e.g. topic timer / close / split notices).

findings.title: Header panel loses all positioning in browsers without flexbox
findings.body: .panel's `float: right` was replaced with `margin-left: auto` plus `@include order(3)` (lines 35-40), and .title's float was removed in favour of .contents being display:flex (lines 14-19). In browsers with no flexbox support at all (e.g. IE9, which the -webkit-box/-moz-box fallbacks in mixins.scss show this codebase still targets with legacy syntax), margin-left:auto/order are inert and nothing floats or positions the panel, so the header icons/login buttons collapse to the left after the title instead of sitting at the right edge. A float fallback (kept alongside the flex rules, since floats are ignored on flex items) is needed.

findings.title: align-items() emits invalid/non-standard legacy values and properties
findings.body: align-items() passes $alignment verbatim to -webkit-box-align, whose 2009-syntax value set is start/end/center/baseline/stretch (not flex-start/flex-end), omits -moz-box-align entirely despite flexbox() emitting -moz-box, and emits -ms-align-items (line 121), which is not a real property (IE10 uses -ms-flex-align, line 120). Current call sites only pass center/baseline so they happen to survive, but as a shared foundation mixin any future align-items(flex-start/flex-end) call will silently do nothing in legacy WebKit and Firefox, producing inconsistent alignment across browsers.
